why: The series' Trash Can is not there in this build: test_117c's ls reports '/mnt/lustre/.lustre/trash/MDT0000: No such file or directory' and the series parent's test_117a fails 'Trash Can not inited on MDT0000' in the same sessions. Only this series fails these tests (branch 0, other uploaders 0), and from ps6 on (and in ps7 and ps14) sanityn 117 never fails again.

bugs.reason: One bug: the trash directory under .lustre is never created (117a's own init check fails right after trash_can_enable=1), so 117b (file not moved into trash) and 117c (tree not in trash) follow from it in every session where they fail together. ps4 was a rebase by a new uploader, the ps14 test reads .lustre/.ltrash, so the bug is likely a trash path or init mismatch between this patch and its series parent, fixed in the next patchset.

notes: 117a and 117b are tests of the series parent, labelled patch-suspect with series_changes 1; 117c is the patch's own test. Grouping by session co-occurrence (all three fail together in every session) would have merged them correctly. patch_changes lists helpers trash_check and trimpath, which only 117c uses, so the patch-changes-test label on 117c is right but the root cause is shared with the parent's tests.

why: sanity-zero is added by this patch, and test_13 'join file works with normal file first' fails its own check 'join should failed' (sanity-zero.sh:368), meaning the join the test expects to be refused succeeded. It fails only on this change (ps30, 31, 32, only in the subtest-change sessions that run it), nowhere else, and later patchsets (33, 35, 39) rewrote the suite (test 13 became test 22) and no longer fail it.

bugs.reason: Single unit: the join code or the new test disagree about joining onto a normal file first; one bug.

notes: patchset_units for ps32 holds only sanity-zero test_13, yet ps32 also fails sanity test_270d 'bad pattern in file 2' 11 times, a series bug (it fails only on 57455 and its parent 57454, ps31 to ps33) that ps30 does carry as a unit. In ps32's evidence 270d shows other_uploaders 2 / other_changes 3, which the 200 day history of the error does not bear out (only 57454 and 57455 fail it, same uploader), and which probably kept it out of the patch class. Also the uploader linked about 70 failures, including fleet wide sanity-lfsck ones (branch_fails 84, 44 uploaders), to the feature ticket LU-18461, so 'covered' by LU-18461 here is not evidence of ambience or of patch fault.

why: test_270d 'DoM: change striping from DoM to RAID0' fails 'bad pattern in file 2' in all 15 sessions that run it, and in 200 days of history it fails only on this change (ps30, ps32) and its series parent 57454 (ps31 to ps33), which adds zero offset (ZEROSTART) layouts, so the layout pattern change of the series is the cause; it was fixed by ps33 of 57455 (no failure in ps33, 35, 39).

bugs.reason: Series bug from the parent 57454's layout pattern change: the DoM to RAID0 migration result no longer reports the expected pattern. Fails on every config.
Separate bug in this patch's own join code or new test: 'join should failed' (the join with a normal file first was not refused). Different suite, different code (join vs pattern), only on 57455.

notes: ps30 has more probable series failures not in patchset_units: sanity 56Ed 'failed to parse old YAML layout' and 56wc 'file data has changed' (15 each), sanity-pfl 2a/2b/11b and sanity-lfsck 18a/18b/18h (6 each). Their elsewhere counts show a few other uploaders, so they were not labelled patch, but they track the same layout feature; the patchset likely holds 3 or more bugs, not 2. The suspect-series stratum here is right, but the cause sits in the parent change, so a predictor scoring 57455's diff alone would miss it: attribution to the series is the right unit.

why: test_34 fails in lfsck_prep with 'rm: cannot remove /mnt/lustre/d23a.sanity-lfsck/d0: Directory not empty', a leftover of test_23a, which failed '(6) only 0 of 4 MDTs are in completed'. The patch rewrites LFSCK start and bookmark handling (new -O mdt-orphan option, bookmark format change); in 200 days these sanity-lfsck signatures fail almost only on this change, on every patchset 3 to 9, and stop at ps10.

bugs.reason: One cascade: on the 4 MDT DNE configs LFSCK fails to start ('Fail to start LFSCK without -M') or never leaves 'init' on remote MDTs ('only 0 of 4 MDTs are in completed'). Each failed test leaves its directory behind, so every later test fails in lfsck_prep with 'Fail to cleanup the env!'. In the same sessions about 35 to 45 sanity-lfsck tests fail; these 13 units are only the ones with no other uploader. All of it stops together at ps10.

A second bug: in sanity 60g the LFSCK run after the aborted transaction injection never completes ('Update not seen after 90s: want completed got init') and leaves subdirs giving 'Bad address', so rmdir fails. 154ea's log is only 'rm: cannot remove /mnt/lustre/d60g.sanity: Directory not empty' and test_cleanup times out on the same leftover: both are cascades of 60g. It is separate from the sanity-lfsck bug because it outlives it: 60g fails on ps3 to ps19 (112 failures, all on this change), 154ea to ps17, while sanity-lfsck is clean from ps10.

notes: 60g is 'covered' through a link to the old LU-7426/EX-12056, but all 112 'rmdir failed' failures in 200 days are on this change: a mislink that would hide a patch bug. The patch_suspect rule picks the subset of a cascade with zero other uploaders: about 13 of some 40 sanity-lfsck failures per session; the rest are 'unmatched' (one other uploader or fleet-wide 'Fail to cleanup the env!' noise), so a predictor is credited with only part of one bug, which is fine if bugs are counted, not units. Two bugs with the same flavour (LFSCK stuck in init) are told apart by the patchset at which each stops failing; per-patchset fix history is a good grouping signal.

why: test_15d fails '(1) only 0 of 4 MDTs are in completed' with lfsck_namespace status 'init' on the other MDTs; the patch changes LFSCK start and the bookmark format, the same sanity-lfsck cascade fails on ps3 to ps9 of this change only (about 8 sessions per patchset, review-dne-part-2 and review-dne-zfs-part-2), and ps10 onward no longer fails it.

bugs.reason: All 9 units (two signatures each for 12b and 15d) are one LFSCK cascade: LFSCK fails to start or never completes on the remote MDTs, and later tests fail on the previous test's leftovers ('Fail to cleanup the env!'). Same core bug as ps5 and ps8, fixed together at ps10.

notes: ps9 still fails sanity 60g, 154ea and test_cleanup (the second bug of this change, LFSCK stuck after 60g's injection, alive until ps19), but they are not in ps9's patchset_units: by ps9 154ea had picked up one failure on another change (other_uploaders 1) and 60g carries a ticket link (LU-7426), so the patch label drops a real patch bug. Labelling a unit as the patch's should consider the change's own history: a test failing on 15 consecutive patchsets of one change and once elsewhere is still that change's bug.

why: 154ea's test log is only 'rm: cannot remove /mnt/lustre/d60g.sanity: Directory not empty': it trips over the directory test_60g left behind after its LFSCK stayed in 'init' and its subdirs returned 'Bad address'. 154ea fails on ps3 to ps17 and 60g on ps3 to ps19 of this change and essentially nowhere else in 200 days (60g: 112 of 112). The passing retest only shows the 60g race is intermittent (60g fails in most, not all, DNE sanity sessions).

bugs.reason: One bug: LFSCK after 60g's aborted transaction injection never completes and leaves damaged dirs; 154ea (rm of d60g) and test_cleanup (Autotest time out on the leftover) are cascades of it. Survives until ps17 to ps19.

The sanity-lfsck cascade: LFSCK fails to start ('Fail to start LFSCK for layout!', 'without -M', 'for namespace') or does not complete on all 4 MDTs, then later tests fail on leftovers. Separate from the 60g bug because it is fixed at ps10 while 60g is not.

notes: suspect-retest-pass is misleading here: the retest passed because the 60g failure is intermittent, not because the failure is ambient. A retest pass should weigh less when the same unit fails on many patchsets of the change and nowhere else. The dataset has 60g, 154ea and test_cleanup as patch units here, but Rainshadow now shows 60g as 'covered' by the old LU-7426 link and 154ea as 'unmatched', so a later relabel would lose the bug; in ps9 it already did. The two LFSCK flavoured bugs could share a root cause, but their fix points differ (ps10 vs ps17 to ps19), so counting them as two is the safe choice.

why: 'lfs mkdir -i0 -c2 ... d56r.sanity: Value too large for defined data type' and the MDS logs 'mdt_create()) bad stripe count 2': ps1 adds an EOVERFLOW range check on lum_stripe_count in mdt_create (with the stripe count made signed) that rejects ordinary 2 and 4 stripe directories. Every DNE sanity and replay-single session of ps1 fails about 217 and 25 tests; ps3 (same day) passes them all and the change merged.

bugs.reason: Sampled 56r, 56bc, 24I, 33j, 51c and replay-single 100a: all fail creating a striped directory with EOVERFLOW, MDS 'bad stripe count N' (2, 4, 2000). 495 units are the generic test_mkdir wrapper failure, which only differ by the random -H hash name in the signature; the rest (24C, 24F, 24I, 31q, 33e, 33f, 33j, 56bc, 56bd, replay-single 100a/100b/110a/110f) are test specific messages for the same rejected striped mkdir.

Probably separate: 'lfs setstripe -o 0,$OSTCOUNT' on a plain file succeeded where it must fail. No directory is created in that test, so the MDT stripe count check does not explain it; it points at the patch's ioctl rework (larger ioctl buffer, consolidated setstripe handling). It fails in all 10 sanity sessions of ps1. The only other change failing it is 63767 (fscrypt), which in Aug/Sep failed the same trio (27Cg, 27Cj, striped mkdir), so the two may share a mechanism; confidence medium.

notes: Units are inflated about 3.5 times: the signature keeps the random dir hash ('-H crush', 'crush2', 'fnv_1a_64', 'all_char'), so one test gives up to 4 units (147 subtests make 510 units). Normalising the -H argument would make the units match subtests. The reverse error is large: in each sanity session about 75 failures with the identical mkdir EOVERFLOW are labelled 'unmatched' or 'ambient-no-ticket' (51c 'Wrong nlink count', 27H, 48b, 56a and others, plus replay-single 100d, 110b to 110g, 116a and ost-pools 32), only because the same generic message was once seen on another change. Session co-occurrence plus the shared log line ('Value too large for defined data type') would group them all as one bug. 27Cj (stripe count 12 != 256) also fails in all ps1 sanity sessions but is labelled unmatched because it fails elsewhere; it may belong with 27Cg.
